newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends steady to higher.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended steady to higher amid ideas that the market was short-term oversold, traders said.
Traders said KCBT wheat hit new contract lows early on hedge selling but bounced back when the selling evaporated.
"We extended our gains as it became clear that Bangladesh will be in next week for 80,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat," a KCBT trader said.
Traders said the Dec/March spread reflected Wednesday's bounce, trading as low as 18-1/2 cents early but widening out to close at 22-1/4 cents.
KCBT wheat settled steady to 4-3/4 cents higher, with Dec up 4-3/4 cents at $3.98-3/4. Earlier, Dec hit a new contract low at $3.93.

Traders said FCC was an early seller of 1.2 million Dec bushels. Benson Quinn was a late buyer, picking up one million each of March and Dec. Benson-Quinn also bull-spread 1.5 million Dec/March at between 18 and 22 cents. General Mills bear-spread one million March/Dec at 20 to 22 cents.
